structure.source: Two conferences of four 4-team divisions, in the real league's alignment. Conference names are placeholders until the Phase 6 naming session.

roster.source: 2020 CBA Article 33 (practice squad eligibility, Section 4; weekly salaries, Section 3) and the league's 2025-26 roster rules as reported by team sites and NFL.com: 90 in the offseason, 53 from the final cutdown, 48 active on game day (47 with fewer than eight offensive linemen), a 16-player practice squad plus one International Player Pathway exemption with up to six players of any experience (2022 on), two game-day elevations per game and three per player per season, four protected practice-squad players a week. Injured reserve: at least four games out, eight designated returns a season (two more in the playoffs), up to two designated at the final cutdown. Reserve/PUP and Reserve/NFI: out at least four games (2024 on). Waivers: players with fewer than four accrued seasons (vested veterans) go on waivers until the trade deadline, everyone after it; claim order follows last season's draft order through Week 3, then current standings (NFL.com 2026-27 calendar).

practiceSquad.weeklySalaryNote: [players with two or fewer accrued seasons, veteran minimum, veteran maximum] per week (CBA Art. 33 Sec. 3). After 2030 the last step's growth continues.

staff.source: NFL Anti-Tampering Policy as reported for the 2023-24 and 2025 hiring cycles (CBS Sports, 'NFL distributes 2023-24 anti-tampering policy'; AP, 'NFL coaching searches have complicated rules about timing and interviews', Jan 7, 2025): another club's assistants may be interviewed (virtually) starting three days after their team's final game; in-person interviews of assistants under contract elsewhere wait until after the divisional round (or their elimination); no coach can sign or agree to a contract until his season is completed. Since 2020 clubs can't block assistants from interviewing for coordinator jobs (league resolution, May 2020). The 2026 policy text wasn't found; these follow the 2025 cycle.

draft.source: Seven rounds; teams hold their picks for the current draft and the next two. Pick clock: 8 minutes in round 1 from 2026 (league notice, December 2025; was 10), 7 in round 2, 5 in rounds 3-6 and compensatory picks, 4 in round 7 (NFL draft procedures as reported for 2025-26). Compensatory picks: CBA Article 6 Sections 2(a) and 10 and Appendix V; tradable since the 2017 draft (owners' resolution). Unrestricted free agents: four or more accrued seasons (Article 9 Section 1(a)).

compensatory.source: CBA Appendix V: compensatory free agents are unrestricted free agents who signed with a new club by the Monday after the draft and rank in the top 35% by Final Numerical Value (average-yearly-compensation rank points, plus 1 point per percentage point of offensive or defensive snaps if 25% or more, kicker 2 per attempt and 1 per make, punter 1 per punt and 1 per punt inside the 20, 20 for first-team All-Pro or 5 for All-Conference). Net loss earns picks after rounds 3-7 by the lost player's percentile; at most 4 per club; an equal loss by count still earns one pick after round 7 when the value lost exceeds the value gained by more than 300 points; no pick before the end of round 5 for a non-quarterback with 10+ accrued seasons. One-year contracts up to $1.75M (2020-21, rising $20,000 every two years) and veteran-salary-benefit deals don't count. Article 6 Section 2(a): at most as many compensatory picks as clubs; fewer are filled with supplemental picks by draft order.

calendar.source: NFL.com 2026 and 2026-27 important dates: tag window Feb 17 to Mar 3, combine Feb 23 to Mar 2, negotiating period from Mar 9, League Year and free agency Mar 11 (4 p.m.), draft Apr 23-25, fifth-year option deadline May 1, preseason weekends Aug 13-15, 20-23 and 27-29, final cutdown to 53 on Sunday Aug 30 (new in 2026: the Sunday after the last preseason game), waiver claims and practice squads Aug 31, Week 1 from Sept 9-10, trade deadline Nov 10 (the Tuesday after Week 9), Week 18 Jan 9-10, championship Feb 14, 2027. Later seasons follow the same rules (2027: draft Apr 29). Training camp opening is approximate (veterans report in late July).

schedule.source: NFL scheduling formula (operations.nfl.com, 2021 17-game announcement). Rotation tables: index 0 is the 2026 season, read from NFL.com's 2026 opponent lists; the other years follow the 3-year (same conference) and 4-year (other conference) cycles. Each other-conference pair is [Conference A division, Conference B division]. The 17th game pairs same-place finishers using the other-conference pairing from two seasons earlier; Conference B hosts it in even years (NFC hosts in 2026). Byes in Weeks 5-14 with at most 6 teams off per week (2025 schedule); Week 18 all division games; trade deadline after Week 9 (2025 deadline Nov 4).

playoffs.source: Seven clubs per conference (four division winners seeded 1-4, three wild cards 5-7); the top seed has a bye; 2v7, 3v6, 4v5; reseeded after the wild-card round so the top seed hosts the lowest remaining seed; higher seed hosts; neutral-site championship.

game.source: NFL rulebook timing rules (15-minute quarters, 3 timeouts per half, two-minute warning, 40-second play clock, clock stops on out-of-bounds plays only in the last 2:00 of the first half and last 5:00 of the second half); extra point snapped from the 15, 2-point try from the 2; dynamic kickoff (2025, kept for 2026): kicked from the 35 into a landing zone from the receiving team's goal line to its 20; kicks into or out of the end zone are touchbacks at the 35, a landing-zone kick downed in the end zone at the 20, short kicks and kicks out of bounds at the 40 (operations.nfl.com dynamic kickoff explainer; 2025 touchback move reported by AP). Onside kicks (owners, March 2026): the kicking team may declare one at any time (2025 allowed it any time only when trailing; no surprise onside kicks); punt touchback to the 20; safety free kick from the 20. Overtime (owners, March 2025): both teams get a possession in the regular season too; regular-season overtime is one 10-minute period with 2 timeouts per team and can end tied; playoff overtime is 15-minute periods, 3 timeouts per two periods, until there is a winner.

penalties.source: NFL rulebook (Rule 14 enforcement; Rules 7, 8, 12): yardage, where it's enforced from, automatic first downs, and loss of down. Simplifications for now: offensive fouls are enforced from the previous spot; pass interference by the defense is a spot foul (at the 1 if in the end zone); personal fouls after a completed play are added to the end of the play; any foul is limited to half the distance to the goal. Which penalties happen, and how often, comes from real data (calibration/matchups.json).

cap.source: 2020 NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement (text read article by article): Article 13 Section 6 (straight-line signing bonus proration, at most 5 years; acceleration on release or trade on or before June 1; up to two June 1 designations per League Year; after June 1 the future years' proration counts next League Year; a new team carries none of a traded player's bonus; Carry Over of Room; LTBE incentives counted, year-end netting; guaranteed future Salary counts at release), Section 6(a)(i) (offseason top 51), Article 26 Section 1 (minimum salaries 2020-2030 by Credited Seasons), Article 12 Section 9 (Minimum Team Cash Spending 90% over 2024-26 and 2027-30), Article 10 (franchise and transition tenders: Cap Percentage Average of the top 5 / top 10 Prior Year Salaries over five years, or 120% of prior salary; third tag 144%), Article 9 Section 2 (RFA tenders grow with the cap), Article 7 Section 7 (fifth-year option tiers). Salary caps: NFL announcements (2026 $301.2M, 2025 $279.2M, 2024 $255.4M, 2023 $224.8M, 2022 $208.2M, 2021 $182.5M, 2020 $198.2M, 2019 $188.2M). 2026 RFA tenders and minimum salaries: NFL Football Operations, Types of Free Agents. 2026 franchise and transition tag values: published table, cross-checked against the amounts NFL.com reported for the four players tagged in 2026 (WR $27.298M, TE $15.045M, RB $14.293M, QB transition $37.833M).
cap.futureGrowthNote: Our projection, not a rule: the cap grew 7.88% into 2026; later years grow by this rate until real figures are added.

minimumSalary.afterAgreementNote: Article 26 schedules end in 2030; later years keep rising by the 2030 step.

veteranSalaryBenefit.note: One-year minimum deals for 4+ credited seasons count at the 2-credited-season minimum. The 2026 bonus allowance is inferred from a reported 2026 contract ($1,262,500 cap charge = $1,075,000 + $187,500).

rookieScale.note: Real 2026 rookie scale: total value above four rookie-minimum salaries (as a share of the 2026 cap) and the signing-bonus share, by overall pick. Totals from every 2026 draft pick's four-year deal; bonus shares from the same slot in 2025 (the 2026 deals' year-by-year detail wasn't published yet). Fitted by `npm run pipeline -- rookies`: interpolating between these knots reproduces every 2026 slot within $40,000. Later drafts scale with the cap.

freeAgency.source: 2020 CBA (overthecap.com's text): Article 8 Section 2 (exclusive rights: fewer than three accrued seasons; tender of a one-year deal at the minimum; may negotiate only with the prior club); Article 9 (restricted: three accrued seasons; tenders with right of first refusal and draft compensation by level; five days to match an offer sheet, no later than one day before the draft; the signing period ends at least five days before the draft; unrestricted: four or more); Article 10 (one franchise or transition designation a year, made from the 22nd to the 8th day before the League Year; a non-exclusive franchise player may negotiate elsewhere for two first-round picks, an exclusive one may not; a transition player only carries a right of first refusal, five days to match; multiyear deals for a franchise player by July 15); Article 7 Section 3(k)(i) (a drafted rookie's contract may not be renegotiated until after his third season's last regular-season game); Article 42 and Exhibit A (training-camp absence fines, mandatory, 2026-30: $60,000 a day, $45,000 for players on rookie contracts).
